title: Fort Hood mass shooter asks judge to halt firing-squad execution set for next week | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Fort Hood mass shooter Nidal Hasan is asking a judge to pause hisexecution by firing squadscheduled for next week.

Attorneys for the former US Army major filed a motion Tuesday in US District Court in Kansas to halt the execution while they mount a legal challenge. They plan to seek habeas corpus — a legal principle that allows people who believe they are being unlawfully detained or imprisoned to petition for their release in court.

The judge has set a hearing on the matter for Wednesday afternoon.

Hasan plans to raise at least two constitutional violations, according to the motion.

“Hasan reserves the right to identify, prepare, and present additional issues once a stay of execution is granted and standby counsel has sufficient opportunity to investigate and research potential claims in order assist him,” his attorneys wrote in the filing.

The former Army psychiatrist was convicted for the 2009 massacre at Fort Hood that left 13 people dead and 32 others wounded.

Hasan’s execution — scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood — will be the US Army’s first such execution of a soldier since World War II and its first imposition of any death penalty on an armed service member in 65 years.

Hasan has been on military death row in Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, while his case proceeds in military court. His petition for a stay of execution was filed in the civilian trial-level federal court.

“There is no question that the violence committed at Fort Hood caused unimaginable pain and loss. But the gravity of that loss does not change the government’s obligation to uphold the principles that define our justice system,” Anna Arceneaux, deputy director of the ACLU’s Capital Punishment Project said in a statement. “Mr. Hasan, like every person facing an irreversible punishment, must have a chance to pursue federal review of his case. We urge the court to stop the government from bypassing Mr. Hasan’s due process rights in its rush to carry out this execution.”

President Donald Trump approved the use of a firing squad for Hasan’s execution, buthe called offDefense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s plans to livestream it.

“I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device,”Trump wroteon Truth Social last month.

CNN previously reported that the president and his advisershad been debatingwhether to call off the Pentagon’s announced plans to livestream the execution, with Trump having remarked privately that he did not initially know that Hasan was paralyzed from the waist down.

Hegseth’s livestream plans immediately received bipartisan backlash and caught people at the Pentagon and Army off guard, CNN reported.

This story has been updated with additional details.
